description: Machine learning for defence and against it: anomaly and intrusion detection, malware and log analytics, then the attacks and defences that arise when an adversary targets the detector. Students train detectors in code, step through networks to see how perturbations work, and evaluate every model against an adaptive attacker.
modelledOn: Sommer and Paxson, Outside the Closed World: On Using Machine Learning for Network Intrusion Detection
Goodfellow, Bengio and Courville, Deep Learning (adversarial examples and regularisation chapters)
MITRE ATT&CK knowledge base and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework
outcomes: Build and evaluate anomaly and supervised detectors for network, host and log data, accounting for class imbalance and base rates.
Extract features for malware and log analytics and explain the drift and obfuscation that degrade them.
Craft evasion, poisoning and extraction attacks under stated threat models and measure their success.
Apply and critically assess defences such as adversarial training, certified bounds and data sanitisation.
Evaluate a detector under adaptive attack and report results that avoid common evaluation errors.

units.title: Anomaly and intrusion detection models
topics: The detection problem: signature versus anomaly detection, and the base-rate fallacy
Intrusion datasets, flow features and class imbalance
Statistical anomaly detection: z-scores, Mahalanobis distance and robust estimators
Isolation forest and one-class SVM
Autoencoders and reconstruction error for anomaly scoring
Supervised detectors: random forest and gradient boosting; precision, recall and ROC analysis

units.title: Malware classification
topics: Static features: byte n-grams, header fields, entropy and strings
Dynamic features: API call sequences and sandbox behaviour reports
Feature hashing and treating binaries as images for convolutional models
Family clustering and classification
Packing, obfuscation and concept drift in malware streams

units.title: Log and event analytics
topics: Log sources: authentication logs, system events, flow records and web access logs
Parsing and normalisation: regular expressions and log template mining
Correlation rules and SIEM concepts; mapping detections to attacker techniques
Sequence models for logs: n-grams, Markov chains and recurrent networks
Graph analytics on authentication data to expose lateral movement
Alert triage, false positive management and analyst workload

units.title: Evasion and poisoning attacks
topics: Threat models: attacker goals, knowledge and capabilities; white-box and black-box
Gradient-based evasion: FGSM and PGD on linear models and neural networks
Problem-space attacks: evading a detector without breaking the malware's function or the packet's validity
Black-box attacks: transferability and query-based search
Data poisoning, label flipping and backdoors
Model extraction and membership inference

units.title: Model robustness and defences
topics: Adversarial training and its cost
Input transformations and gradient masking: why many defences fail
Certified robustness: randomised smoothing and interval bounds
Robust feature design and monotonic constraints
Poisoning defences: data sanitisation, robust statistics and provenance
Ensembles, adversarial input detection and defence in depth

units.title: Threat intelligence mining
topics: Threat intelligence sources and formats: indicators, STIX and TAXII, ATT&CK techniques
Extracting indicators and entities from reports with text mining
Clustering and linking campaigns from shared infrastructure and behaviour
Detecting phishing, mobile money fraud SMS and scam content
Enrichment, scoring and sharing of indicators

units.title: Evaluating detectors under attack
topics: Metrics at low base rates: precision-recall curves, cost-sensitive evaluation and alert budgets
Temporal evaluation and drift: time-split testing instead of random splits
Adaptive attacks and evaluation checklists for defences
Robust accuracy curves and attack budgets
Red-team and blue-team exercises as evaluation
Reproducible evaluation and honest reporting

units.title: Responsible deployment and project
topics: Privacy and legal limits of security analytics, including monitoring staff and customers
Dual-use research ethics and disclosure of model vulnerabilities
Project: build and break a detector against an adaptive attacker
Project presentation and critique

schedule.title: The detection problem and statistical anomalies
schedule.exercise: A detector has 99 percent true positive and 1 percent false positive rates and attacks occur in 1 in 10,000 flows: compute the probability that an alert is real, and explain what this means for analysts.

tasks.title: Compute precision of an alert for several attack base rates with fixed true and false positive rates and plot the collapse at low rates
Flag outliers in login-count features with z-scores and Mahalanobis distance and compare which catches a planted attacker faster
Build flow features from a labelled capture, handle 1 percent attack imbalance with weighting, and compare detection with and without it

schedule.title: Machine learning detectors and evaluation
schedule.exercise: Compare an isolation forest, an autoencoder and a random forest on the same intrusion data, choose an alert threshold for a team that can review 50 alerts a day, and justify the choice.

tasks.title: Train an isolation forest on normal flows only, score a mixed test set, and report which attack types are found
Train a small autoencoder on benign traffic, set a threshold from reconstruction error, and report false positives on a held-out day
Train a random forest and boosted trees, plot ROC and precision-recall curves, and pick the threshold that meets an alert budget of 50 per day

schedule.title: Malware features and classification
schedule.exercise: Describe the features you would extract from a Windows executable and from its sandbox report, explain how packing hides them, and design a test that shows drift over six months.

tasks.title: Compute byte-histogram and entropy features for a set of benign and sample files and plot which separate the classes
Classify programs from API call n-gram counts with logistic regression and report accuracy with a confusion matrix
Train on the first three months of samples, test on the next three, and measure how much accuracy falls as families change

schedule.title: Log sources, parsing and correlation
schedule.exercise: Parse 10,000 authentication log lines into templates and fields, write three correlation rules for brute force, password spraying and impossible travel, and map each to an attacker technique.

tasks.title: Write regular expressions to parse authentication log lines into time, user, source address and result, and count malformed lines
Group 5,000 unstructured log lines into templates by masking variable tokens and report the top ten templates by frequency
Implement three correlation rules over parsed events, run them on logs with planted attacks, and measure detections and false alerts

schedule.title: Sequences, graphs and alert triage
schedule.exercise: Model normal command sequences with a Markov chain, build a user-to-host graph from logins to spot an account moving laterally, and propose a triage score that reduces analyst workload.

tasks.title: Estimate a Markov chain over system call types from normal traces and score unseen traces by log-likelihood
Build a user-to-host login graph, find a path of new logins from a compromised account, and rank hosts by reachability
Triage a queue of 30 alerts in a scenario under a time limit, justify each priority, and measure missed true incidents

schedule.title: Threat models and gradient-based evasion
schedule.exercise: State a threat model for an attacker evading a spam and fraud SMS filter, derive the FGSM perturbation for logistic regression, and explain why changing features is not the same as changing a real message.

tasks.title: Step through a small neural network, compute the gradient with respect to the input, and see a prediction flip from a small perturbation
Implement FGSM against a logistic regression detector and plot accuracy as the perturbation budget grows from 0 to 0.3
Attack a flow classifier while keeping packet counts and byte totals consistent, and compare success with the unconstrained attack

schedule.title: Black-box attacks, poisoning and model theft
schedule.exercise: Plan a poisoning attack that flips 5 percent of training labels to hide one attack family, and describe how a query-limited attacker can steal a decision boundary.

tasks.title: Flip 5, 10 and 20 percent of training labels at random and plot the detector's recall on a clean test set
Craft adversarial examples on a surrogate model and measure how often they transfer to a different target classifier
Query a prediction API with a budget of 2,000 queries, train a copy, and measure agreement between the copy and the original

schedule.title: Adversarial training and certified robustness
schedule.exercise: Argue why a defence that obscures gradients can still be broken, and compute a randomised smoothing radius for a classifier from its top-class probability.

tasks.title: Retrain a classifier on its own FGSM examples and compare clean accuracy and robust accuracy before and after
Add input quantisation as a defence, show it stops FGSM, then bypass it with a different attack and explain why
Estimate a smoothed classifier's certified radius by Monte Carlo sampling for ten inputs and plot certified accuracy against radius

schedule.title: Robust features, poisoning defences and defence in depth
schedule.exercise: Rank features by how much an attacker can change them cheaply, build a detector that relies on hard-to-change ones, and design a layered pipeline that combines a model, rules and an adversarial input check.

tasks.title: Remove suspicious training points by distance to class medians and show that recall under poisoning recovers
Train a detector on only features that are costly to change and compare its evasion success to the full-feature model
Combine a classifier, a rule layer and an anomaly check, then measure the attack budget needed to defeat each layer in turn

schedule.title: Mining threat intelligence and fraud content
schedule.exercise: Extract indicators and techniques from five incident reports, cluster them into campaigns, and build a classifier for fraudulent mobile money SMS messages.

tasks.title: Extract IP addresses, domains and file hashes from ten report excerpts with regular expressions and count unique indicators
Train a text classifier on labelled SMS messages to separate scam from genuine mobile money notices and report precision and recall
Link indicators that share infrastructure into a graph, cluster it into campaigns, and describe each cluster using ATT&CK techniques

schedule.title: Metrics, time and adaptive attacks
schedule.exercise: Show how a random train-test split overstates a detector's performance compared with a time-ordered split, and list five checks a defence evaluation must pass before its claims are trusted.

tasks.title: Plot a precision-recall curve for a detector on 0.1 percent attack data and compare its area with the ROC area
Evaluate the same detector with random and time-ordered splits and report how much the performance drops under the honest split
Design an adaptive attack that knows the defence in a given paper-style setup and measure how much it lowers the reported robust accuracy

schedule.title: Robustness curves, red teams and reproducibility
schedule.exercise: Produce a robust accuracy curve for your best detector, plan a red-team exercise against it, and write a reproducibility checklist covering data, seeds and splits.

tasks.title: Plot robust accuracy against perturbation size for a detector with and without adversarial training on one chart
Play the blue team in a scenario: observe an adaptive attacker's moves, update detections between rounds, and score the outcome
Re-run an evaluation from a fixed seed and data version on a clean environment, and report any differences from the first run

schedule.title: Ethics, deployment and project
schedule.exercise: Present a detector built to protect a mobile money service, show how a determined attacker defeats or fails to defeat it, and state the privacy limits of the data you used.

tasks.title: Decide in a case whether an employer may analyse staff email for threats, balancing privacy law, necessity and proportionality
Handle the discovery of a bypass for a widely deployed detector in a case, choosing disclosure steps and timing
Build a detector, attack it with a white-box evasion, defend it, and attack again with an adaptive attack, reporting results at each stage
